target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28 with AWS, Capital One, Amazon contract and UMIACS research — strong brands, but four concurrent 'Present' roles and a wall of bolded AWS service names.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Results often trail long tech chains; several bullets (Fine-tuning, Leo deploy, AWS intern) have no outcome at all, only plumbing.
score_rationale.quantification: Numbers exist but baselines are fuzzy: '34% speedup' of what, '90% satisfaction report compared to legacy', '93%' of how many testers.
score_rationale.technical_depth: Real techniques present (precomputed index, LSM vs B+ tree, rdtscp), but many bullets are AWS service chains rather than decisions.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Many 3-line bullets, run-on 'with ... with ...' clauses, and 3–6 bolded terms per bullet; bold shouts instead of guiding.
score_rationale.skim_test: Brands and titles visible; headline wins buried at end of 3-line bullets; heavy bold dilutes what matters.
score_rationale.credibility: Overlapping roles (Amazon contract, AWS intern, UMIACS, TerpLabs all 'Present'; project during Capital One) invite 'how many hours?' questions; puffed verbs.
score_rationale.ats_parseability: Clean extraction, but phone is a placeholder '(XXX) XXX-XXXX'; skills misfile SQS under observability, CloudFormation under CI/CD.
score_rationale.visual_layout: One page, but cramped: dense bullets, small margins, Certifications breaks flow before Experience; bold noise everywhere.
score_rationale.domain_fit: Good brands for general SWE, but cloud-plumbing bullets outweigh core engineering; AWS intern role nearly empty at top.
score_rationale.overall: Brands will earn interviews, but a skeptical interviewer will poke holes in overlap, unanchored metrics, and skills breadth (Rust, CUDA, K8s unsupported).

must_fix: Replace placeholder phone '(XXX) XXX-XXXX' with a real number or remove it.

clarify: concurrent timelines — Amazon contract (Jan 2026–Present), AWS SDE intern (Sep–Dec 2026), UMIACS (Present), TerpLabs (Present), and the IEX project during the Capital One internship. Mark part-time or end dates honestly.
clarify: baselines for '34% speedup' (latency? throughput? vs. what prior design), '90% internal satisfaction report compared to the legacy tool', and '93% meal satisfaction' (how many test users).
Cut 3-line bullets to ≤2 lines and reduce bolding to 1–2 anchors per bullet.
Prune skills you can't defend in an interview from bullets (Rust, CUDA, Kubernetes/EKS, Spring Boot, Pinecone/LlamaIndex); fix miscategorized SQS and CloudFormation.
AWS SDE intern entry has one vague present-tense bullet at the top of Experience; either say concretely what you're working on or keep it brief without filler.

bullets.quote: Researching and implementing Java-based utilization optimizations for
bullets.issue: Vague 'researching and implementing optimizations'; no scope of what is being optimized.
bullets.suggestion: clarify: which Redshift component/resource the utilization work targets; otherwise keep as a short, honest in-progress line.

bullets.quote: Overhauled the legacy UI of a test data
bullets.issue: 3-line run-on; 'internal satisfaction report of 90% compared to legacy' is ambiguous.
bullets.suggestion: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow editor in React + Electron (TypeScript, React-Flow) with Jest-tested state validation; clarify what the 90% satisfaction figure measures.

bullets.quote: Engineered a lightweight tree-style workflow search index
bullets.issue: Good design choice buried; no result stated; Redis + Node IPC tail is tech padding.
bullets.suggestion: Built a precomputed tree-style search index over a 270K-row PostgreSQL workflow table (Python/SQLAlchemy) to cut DB queries under access constraints, with Redis caching for full retrieval.

bullets.quote: Developed a Claude skill for workflow generation,
bullets.issue: Strong result (65%, <15s) buried after long chain; 'previous tooling' baseline vague.
bullets.suggestion: Cut workflow generation time 65% (to <15s) vs. prior tooling by building a Claude skill with sub-skill decomposition and Python validators; profiled via CloudWatch/OpenSearch latency logs.

bullets.quote: Deployed an Amazon Leo space topic research
bullets.issue: 'Adopted into Leo's ecosystem' is unverifiable puffery; no who/how-many; what the utility does is unclear.
bullets.suggestion: Deployed a research utility for Amazon Leo on Docker + Fargate with GitHub Actions CI/CD and CDK (TypeScript) infra so unfamiliar engineers could contribute. clarify: who adopted it.

bullets.quote: Achieved a 34% speedup on a pipeline routing
bullets.issue: 'Speedup' metric and baseline undefined; final clause is service name-dropping.
bullets.suggestion: Sped up a 6,000+ document inference pipeline 34% [clarify: latency/throughput vs. prior design] by moving to Kinesis streams feeding Lambda processors behind API Gateway.

bullets.quote: Integrated automated fine-tuning of an AWS Bedrock
bullets.issue: Pure AWS service chain, 3 lines, no outcome; 'decision gates' is the only interesting part.
bullets.suggestion: Automated retraining of a Bedrock relevance model via EventBridge schedules with decision gates to skip redundant runs; added X-Ray tracing and SNS failure alerts.

bullets.quote: Developing automated training for PhysTwin, a physics-based
bullets.issue: 'Targeting an ICLR submission' is aspiration, fine if honest; your contribution is vague.
bullets.suggestion: Developing automated training for PhysTwin (physics-based digital twin) with a PhD-led team; work aimed at an ICLR submission.

bullets.quote: Built a Python pipeline linking AnyGrasp multi-camera
bullets.issue: 'Enabling researchers to develop changes faster' is generic filler; full model name is noise.
bullets.suggestion: Built a Python pipeline feeding AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp candidates into Open3D-rendered overlays for a Qwen3-VL model, letting researchers isolate scene components.

bullets.quote: Cut research-environment setup time 30% via UV
bullets.issue: Setup time result is fine; psutil/Pytest tail is unrelated to setup and muddles causation.
bullets.suggestion: Cut research-environment setup time 30% with uv dependency pinning and Docker for reproducible setups; added psutil timing/memory monitoring and Pytest tests.

bullets.quote: Co-founded and scaled a 110+ member campus
bullets.issue: 'Scaled' + 'agile practices' + Jira/GitHub bolded reads like LLM puffery; tools add nothing.
bullets.suggestion: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that has shipped 5 live products; organize teams and code review via Jira and GitHub.

bullets.quote: Sustained 20,000+ site visits within the initial
bullets.issue: Implies your SQL/Redis work caused the traffic; visits came from product, not caching.
bullets.suggestion: Built Prisma SQL queries with Redis caching for Tortuga, a class scheduler that drew 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, to reduce database load and latency.

bullets.quote: Building a work-in-progress integration of a RAG
bullets.issue: Honestly scoped WIP—good; '93% satisfaction' lacks sample size; 'official' bolded is overselling.
bullets.suggestion: Building (WIP) a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the UMD app with GPT-4o mini over ChromaDB + SentenceBERT; clarify: number of internal testers behind 93%.

bullets.quote: Implemented a C++-based order book simulation on
bullets.issue: 'Contract-based plug-and-play design ... enforced correctness' is vague; what's enforced?
bullets.suggestion: Implemented a C++ order book simulator on historical IEX data with a pluggable interface so multiple matching/storage designs can be swapped and checked for correctness.

bullets.quote: Wrote and evaluated paginated hash-based data storage
bullets.issue: 'Evaluated' twice, no result; what was the drift finding?
bullets.suggestion: Built paginated hash-based storage for live book data with an LFU cache for hot tickers; validated drift against IEX historical book. clarify: outcome of the evaluation.

bullets.quote: Designed and assessed the performance of a time-based
bullets.issue: Good, interview-worthy methodology (rdtscp, perf) but no finding reported.
bullets.suggestion: Benchmarked a time-based adaptive LSM vs. a B+ tree for log storage using rdtscp timing and Linux perf counters. clarify: which won and by how much.
